# The agent

You are a Seon agent: you work one task at a Clojure REPL on your own branch, and every change you make is a form you evaluate.

This page is what every agent reads first, and `(my.agent/help)` lists its sections again; `(my.agent/help "done")` shows one whole. Every single-backticked form on it runs in an agent as written (`seon.repl-test/the-help-page-runs`); a double-backticked one is a pattern to fill in.

## Your turn

You have one tool, eval: call it with Clojure forms, and you see what the REPL answered before your next call.

- Evaluate a little, read the answer, then take the next step. Prose inside your code goes in `;;` comments, and text outside an eval call is never evaluated.
- Identical forms with identical answers are folded into one, headed by how many times they repeated (`;; 24x`).
- An unbalanced delimiter is repaired, and the repair is shown to you next turn under `:your-last-reply`, as is a reply cut at the model's token limit.
- Every cut in what you read names the form that reads its rest. Your last turn's evaluations in full: `(my.turn/evals)`.

## What you read

Your context comes in two parts: the run's, sent once and unchanged while you work, then the turn's, measured again after each of your replies.

The run's part:
- `:task`: its id, kind and instructions, and its plan as it accumulated along its needs, prerequisites first.
- `:references`: each var the plan cites, at the depth its delimiter asks (`docs/references.md#the-delimiter-picks-the-depth`): a bare name its arglists and first sentence, one backtick its doc and contract, three its source. A source past the cap shows `:left-out` and `:read`, the form that reads it.
- `:found`: program functions the cited vars and your proofs call that the plan does not name, and the program forms nearest the plan in meaning; often the helpers the task needs.
- `:map`: the functions of the namespaces your proofs and cited vars live in, a line each (name, arglists, first sentence), most used first; ``(clojure.repl/dir the.ns)`` lists them all. Before writing a helper, look here for one.
- `:sections`: the wiki sections, files and namespaces the plan cites, at their depth.
- `:evidence`: why the last run on this branch was refused (`:problem`) and what it measured: conflicts, unmerged keys, red proofs. Root held the task and released it again here, on the same branch, so its work is yours to continue.

The turn's part:
- `:turn`: this turn of the most you have.
- `:proofs`: each of your proofs and its status. A red one shows each failure as `:assert` (as written) and `:got` (what it evaluated to), its source, and `:calls`, the program functions it calls. `:undefined` is not written yet, `:not-run` means the test run failed (see `:test-run`), `:no-assertions` means it ran and asserted nothing.
- `:refused`: what keeps you from done beyond your red proofs (the done rule, `seon.reconcile/done-explain`): `:regression` (green on main, red here: your change broke it), `:stray-red` (a red test that is no task's proof), `:contract-gap` (a function you defined without a ``:malli/schema``), `:open-problem` (a problem your own work made true, such as a citation of a var you deleted: `seon.problems/caused`), `:proof-unknown` (a proof with no result: it never ran), `:unmerged` (a merge entry not resolved), `:no-proofs`, and on a design task `:no-design` (your plan is unchanged since the run began; it shows the form that changes it).
- `:test-run`: the test run itself failing (a timeout, a dead fork); no test result is real until it runs.
- `:unmerged`: on a merge task, the entries to resolve.
- `:attention`: the wiki sections your code changes made stale, to read and probably fix; never a reason to refuse done.
- `:will-merge`: every change your branch's merge will carry to main: the vars you added, changed and removed, and the schemas you registered or changed; `{}` when it carries nothing. Anything listed that the task does not need, put back.
- `:tests`: how many tests this turn ran (`:this-turn`: your proofs and the tests your branch changed), how many root's judge runs at your run's end (`:at-judge`, `(my.agent/prove)` runs the same), and `:when-asked`: tests your change reaches that start a process of their own (a shell, a fork, a root). Those never run in your turn or the judge unless one is a proof of your task; root runs the others when it asks. `(my.agent/deferred)` lists them.
- `:messages`: what was sent to you since your last turn, each `{:from :body}`: the owner's words (`:from "owner"`), root's, or another agent's (its run id). The owner's is a fact (`:seon.message/*`) your turn writes on your branch, and every later reading of the turn reads it again from that commit.
- Your last evaluations, when no earlier turn shows them.

## The REPL

This is a real Clojure REPL: what you define becomes part of your branch's program exactly as written.

- Your work is Clojure forms evaluated here. Think in `;;` comments right before each form: what it is for, what you expect it to show. The comments are recorded with the form's evaluation (a definition keeps them as its leading comment), and the owner reads them beside each form and its result. The eval tool's optional `thinking` says why the whole call.

- `(ns app.workout)` creates a namespace (with its `:require`s) and it becomes part of your program; ``(in-ns 'the.ns)`` then ``(defn f ...)`` changes an existing one, and its callers see it at once.
- Every function you define needs a Malli contract in its metadata: `(defn total {:malli/schema [:=> [:cat [:vector :int]] :int]} [xs] (reduce + 0 xs))`.
- Your own namespace is scratch and never merges: `(in-ns (symbol (str "agent." (name (:id (my.agent/whoami))))))`. There the `my.*` functions are referred unqualified; elsewhere call them qualified, as written here.
- A schema changes as a function does, on your branch: `(my.schema/register! :app.workout/set [:map [:reps :int] [:kg :double]])`; your next forms see it. To change an existing key, start from its form: `(get (my.schema/forms) :seon.task/task)`.
- Your branch's program is the forms you evaluate, recorded on your branch; the files in the checkout are not your branch. Writing a file under src or test, or running git, changes the shared checkout under every agent and root, not your program: a file is an effect, through its owner.
- An earlier result: ``(my.agent/$ :h3)`` by its handle, or `*1`; the last error is `*e`, and ``(my.agent/pst)`` prints it with its causes.

## Finding your way

The program as your branch records it answers where things are, so read before you write.

- By name: `(clojure.repl/apropos "accumulate")`; by docstring: `(clojure.repl/find-doc "accumulated plan")`; by the text of a definition: `(my.agent/grep "accumulated")`.
- A function: `(clojure.repl/doc seon.task/accumulate)` and `(clojure.repl/source seon.task/accumulate)`; who calls it: `(my.agent/callers 'seon.task/accumulate)`; what it calls: `(my.agent/callees 'seon.task/accumulate)`.
- A namespace's ns form, its requires and aliases (to write a test where its siblings are): `(clojure.repl/source seon.task)`.
- A namespace's publics: `(clojure.repl/dir my.task)`; every program namespace: `(my.db/q '[:find [?n ...] :where [_ :ns/name ?n]])`.
- Your task: `(my.task/current)`; one task by id: `(seon.task/task (my.db/db) (:seon.task/id (my.task/current)))`.
- An effect (a file, a model, git) goes through its owner: ``(my.fx/call :kind req)``.

## Done

Your task is done when every proof passes and the done rule refuses nothing; the proofs run after each of your replies. A run that ends refused (a red or unrun proof, a reason, no progress, a dead agent, a refused merge) is not retried: its task is held for root, which decides whether to run it again (`docs/tasks.md#a-refused-run-is-held-for-root`).

- A proof is a deftest in a test namespace: `(ns app.workout-test (:require [clojure.test :refer [deftest is]] [app.workout :as w]))`, then `(deftest total-sums (is (= 6 (w/total [1 2 3]))))`, run with `(clojure.test/run-tests 'app.workout-test)`.
- A cost proof (`seon.cost/proof`) is your performance goal: it says what N counts, the least work the data needs (`:work`, e.g. one pass with one lookup per row), how that grows and what it may cost. Read it before writing code and do no more work than it states.
- Run what judges your branch now, as root's judge does: ``(my.agent/prove)`` runs your proofs and every test your change reaches, reusing each one green at its reach digest, and answers `:results`.
- The judge counts exactly (`seon.cost/slack`): allocated bytes may reach 1.25x the estimate, contracted calls 1.0x and ticks (the counted time dimension) 3x. CPU time (`:ns`) is measured and shown ("TIME OVER") but never red. A dimension whose growth exponent exceeds `:growth`'s by more than `seon.cost/steeper-by` (0.3) is STEEPER (an extra pass), red even inside the slack; LOOSE (a third of the estimate or less) is not red. Its failure message prints measured over estimate per size.

## Merging

A merge task's branch has main merged in, and each of its unmerged entries shows `:base`, `:ours` and `:theirs`.

- `(my.branch/unmerged)` lists them. Resolve one by redefining the var with the content both sides need, or keep one side: ``(my.branch/resolve! 'ns/var :theirs)``, or ``(my.branch/resolve! 'ns/var)`` to keep yours.
- Your branch sees only its own changes until then.

## Ending

Record what you learned in the plan, so the next step starts from it, then stop.

- `(my.task/update! :seon.task/plan str "\n\nFound: seon.task/accumulate owns the plan's accumulation.")`.
- When the task cannot be done as planned, fail it with the form that shows why: `(my.task/fail! "the premise is refuted" '(seon.task/accumulate {} "x"))`. The failure goes on the task, your run ends, and the task is held for root (`docs/tasks.md#a-refused-run-is-held-for-root`).
- `(my.turn/wait)` ends your turn and waits for root.
I'll start by reading the current state of the relevant code.

  \"A method's identity: [multi dispatch], printed.\"

{:printed "nil",
 :form "(clojure.repl/source seon.program/remove-definition!)",
 :out
   "(defn- remove-definition!
  \"Make this process hold no definition for program key k (a var unmapped, a method
  removed).\"
  {:malli/schema [:=> [:cat :any] :any]}
  [[kind a b]]
  (case kind
    :var (when-let [n (find-ns (symbol (namespace a)))] (ns-unmap n (symbol (name a))))
    :method (when-let [v (find-var a)] (when (instance? clojure.lang.MultiFn @v) (remove-method @v (read-string b))))
    nil))
"}

{:printed "nil",
 :form "(clojure.repl/source seon.program/def-eid)",
 :out
   "(defn def-eid
  \"The entity of definition key k ([:var v], [:method multi dispatch], [:impl protocol type],
  [:ns n]) on db, or nil.\"
  {:malli/schema [:=> [:cat :seon.host/db :any] [:maybe :int]]}
  [db [kind a b]]
  (let [[attr v] (case kind :var [:var/name a] :method [:method/key (method-key a b)]
                       :impl [:impl/key (impl-key a b)] :ns [:ns/name a])]
    (pdb/eid db attr v)))
"}

{:printed "nil",
 :form "(clojure.repl/source seon.program/def-ref)",
 :out
   "(defn def-ref
  \"The entity map naming definition k: e, its entity (def-eid) when the db has it, else an
  upsert by its identity with its tempid (Datahike allocates a tempid first seen as a ref,
  in :form/defines, before the map that upserts it, and a form defining two existing
  definitions, a protocol or a record, then conflicts).\"
  {:malli/schema [:=> [:cat :any [:maybe :int]] :map]}
  [[kind a b] e]
  (cond-> (case kind
            :var {:db/id (var-tid a) :var/name a :var/ns (ns-tid (symbol (namespace a)))}
            :method (let [k (method-key a b)] {:db/id (str \"method \" k) :method/key k :method/multi a :method/dispatch b})
            :impl (let [k (impl-key a b)] {:db/id (str \"impl \" k) :impl/key k :impl/protocol a :impl/type b})
            :ns {:db/id (ns-tid a) :ns/name a})
    e (assoc :db/id e)))
"}

{:printed "nil",
 :form "(clojure.repl/source seon.program/def-tx)",
 :out
   "(defn def-tx
  \"tx-data making definition k point at the form content names (content {:form :kind
  :contract :doc :file}), retracting what it held that content does not, or, for nil
  content, retracting what it held. e: its entity on db (def-eid), or nil.\"
  {:malli/schema [:=> [:cat :seon.host/db :any [:maybe :int] [:maybe :map]] :seon.db/tx-data]}
  [db k e content]
  (let [x (when e (d/entity db e))
        attrs (case (first k) :var [:var/form :var/kind :var/contract :var/doc] :ns [:ns/form :ns/file] [(pointer (first k))])
        now (when content
              (cond-> {(pointer (first k)) (form-tid (:form content))}
                (:kind content) (assoc :var/kind (:kind content))
                (:contract content) (assoc :var/contract (:contract content))
                (:doc content) (assoc :var/doc (:doc content))
                (:file content) (assoc :ns/file (:file content))))]
    (into (if content [(merge (def-ref k e) now) {:db/id (form-tid (:form content)) :form/id (:form content)}] [])
          (for [a attrs :let [old (get x a)] :when (and (some? old) (not (contains? now a)))]
            [:db/retract e a (if ((set (vals pointer)) a) (:db/id old) old)]))))
"}

{:printed "nil",
 :form "(clojure.repl/source seon.stage/stage-tx)",
 :out
   "(defn stage-tx
  \"tx-data making branch db's definitions match this live runtime: each var recorded with a
  form in a loaded namespace and no longer interned there, and each recorded method its
  multimethod no longer has, stops pointing to its form.\"
  {:malli/schema [:=> [:cat :seon.host/db] :seon.db/tx-data]}
  [db]
  ;; one pass over the recorded vars' names and one ns-interns per namespace (it builds the
  ;; namespace's whole map), never one per var
  (let [names (into {} (map (juxt :e :v)) (d/datoms db :aevt :var/name))
        vars (for [dt (d/datoms db :aevt :var/form)] [dt (names (:e dt))])
        interns (into {} (for [nsym (distinct (map (comp symbol namespace second) vars))
                               :let [n (find-ns nsym)] :when n]
                           [nsym (ns-interns n)]))]
  (vec (concat
         (for [[dt sym] vars
               :let [in (interns (symbol (namespace sym)))]
               :when (and in (not (get in (symbol (name sym)))))]
           [:db/retract (:e dt) :var/form (:v dt)])
         (for [dt (d/datoms db :aevt :method/form)
               :let [m (d/entity db (:e dt)) v (find-var (:method/multi m))]
               :when (and v (instance? clojure.lang.MultiFn @v)
                          (not (contains? (methods @v) (read-string (:method/dispatch m)))))]
           [:db/retract (:e dt) :method/form (:v dt)])))))
"}

   "(ns seon.program-test
  \"The program as the compiler knows it (owner, 2026-10-21; inv4's design): each form an
  agent evaluates is recorded with what Jolt's analyzer says it defines, declares and
  references (jolt.analyzer/*unit-tap*) and a readback of what it set, never from its text.
  Every kind of definition (defn, defmulti and defmethod, defprotocol and extend-type,
  defrecord, do-nested defs, a new namespace's ns form); scratch namespaces stay scratch; a
  redefinition supersedes the form it replaces and takes its place; main loads forms in the
  order of their real references; a test reaches what it calls; banned calls and inline
  definitions are recorded for the merge to judge; a file analyzed without running gives
  the REPL's facts.\"
  (:require [seon.test-store :as ts] [clojure.test :refer [deftest is testing]]
            [datahike.api :as d]
            [seon.db :as pdb]
            [seon.program :as program]
            [seon.proofs :as proofs]
            [seon.fx :as fx]
            [seon.merge :as pm]
            [seon.source :as source]
            [clojure.java.shell :as sh]
            [test-runner :as runner]
            [jolt.analyzer]))
"}

{:printed "nil",
 :form "(clojure.repl/source seon.program/form-tx)",
 :out
   "(defn form-tx
  \"Form id as one entity map, from row (a form's account or a merge's form content): its
  text, namespace, order and lead, the definitions and declarations it names (def-ref's ids,
  each definition's entity read from eid-of: a map, or def-eid on the db) and its form-sets.\"
  {:malli/schema [:=> [:cat :string :map ifn?] :map]}
  [id {:keys [ns src order lead defines declares] :as row} eid-of]
  (into (cond-> {:db/id (form-tid id) :form/id id :form/src src :form/ns (ns-tid ns) :form/order order}
          lead (assoc :form/lead lead)
          (seq defines) (assoc :form/defines (mapv #(:db/id (def-ref % (eid-of %))) defines))
          (seq declares) (assoc :form/declares (mapv #(:db/id (def-ref [:var %] (eid-of [:var %]))) declares)))
        (for [[a k] form-sets :let [v (get row k)] :when (seq v)] [a (vec v)])))
"}

{:printed "nil",
 :form "(clojure.repl/source seon.program/unit-account)",
 :out
   "(defn unit-account
  \"What the compiler says one analyzed top-level node does, from its IR by resolved var
  identity: the vars it defines at its top (:defs, each def-info) and inside a function body
  (:inline-defs), its multimethod methods ({:multi sym-as-written :dispatch value}) and
  protocol extensions ({:protocol sym :type name}), the multimethods it sets up, the vars and
  host statics (Class/member) it references (:refs, with the vars its quoted data names:
  quoted-vars), the banned vars it references, the
  calls it bounds by a clock (:timeouts: deref with a timeout), its catch clauses
  (:catches, each {:class :answers}), the namespaces it requires, and whether it changes its
  namespace's environment (:env?).\"
  {:malli/schema [:=> [:cat :map] :map]}
  [node]
  (let [acc (volatile! {:defs [] :inline-defs #{} :methods [] :impls [] :multis #{} :refs #{} :banned #{} :requires #{} :env? false
                        :timeouts #{} :catches #{}})]
    ((fn walk [n in-fn?]
       (case (:op n)
         :def (if in-fn?
                (vswap! acc update :inline-defs conj (vsym n))
                (vswap! acc update :defs conj (def-info n)))
         :defmacro (if in-fn?
                     (vswap! acc update :inline-defs conj (vsym n))
                     (vswap! acc update :defs conj {:var (vsym n) :meta {} :macro? true :init :fn}))
         (:var :the-var) (let [s (vsym n)]
                           (when (banned s) (vswap! acc update :banned conj s))
                           (vswap! acc update :refs conj s))
         :host-static (vswap! acc update :refs conj (symbol (str (:class n)) (str (:member n))))
         ;; a scalar names no var unless it is a qualified symbol: most constants (keywords,
         ;; strings, numbers) cost no walk
         (:quote :const) (let [x (datum n)]
                           (when (or (coll? x) (qualified-symbol? x))
                             (vswap! acc update :refs into (quoted-vars x))))
         :try (vswap! acc update :catches into (map sedn/encode) (catches n))
         :invoke (when (and (= 'clojure.core/deref (invoked n)) (= 3 (count (:args n))))
                   (vswap! acc update :timeouts conj 'clojure.core/deref))
         nil)
       (case (:op n)
         :invoke (when-not in-fn?
                   (let [f (invoked n) args (:args n)]
                     (case f
                       clojure.core/defmethod-setup
                       (vswap! acc update :methods conj {:multi (datum (first args)) :dispatch (datum (second args))})
                       clojure.core/register-method
                       (vswap! acc update :impls conj {:type (str (datum (first args))) :protocol (symbol (str (datum (second args))))})
                       clojure.core/defmulti-setup
                       (vswap! acc update :multis conj (datum (first args)))
                       (when (env-calls f)
                         (vswap! acc assoc :env? true)
                         (when ('#{clojure.core/require clojure.core/use} f)
                           (vswap! acc update :requires into (mapcat (comp libs unquote-form datum)) args))))))
         nil)
       (let [in-fn? (or in-fn? (#{:fn :defmacro} (:op n)))]
         (ir/reduce-ir-children (fn [_ c] (walk c in-fn?)) nil n)))
     node false)
    @acc))
"}

{:printed "nil",
 :form "(clojure.repl/source seon.program/account-tx)",
 :out
   "(defn account-tx
  \"The facts of a form's account on db: the form (keeping its order when it is already
  there, else taking the place of the forms it supersedes, else after every form: order
  next-order), each definition pointing to it (def-tx), and the forms it supersedes
  retracted (each whose every definition it redefines). An account names no definition it
  lacks: a text form's is its id, text, namespace, lead and order.\"
  {:malli/schema [:=> [:cat :seon.host/db :map :int] :seon.db/tx-data]}
  [db {:keys [id ns ns-form? defs declares order] :as acct} next-order]
  (let [fe (pdb/eid db :form/id id)
        dkeys (def-keys acct)
        eids (into {} (for [k (into dkeys (map #(vector :var %)) declares)] [k (def-eid db k)]))
        des (set (keep eids dkeys))
        olds (disj (set (keep #(form-of db %) des)) fe nil)
        superseded (filterv (fn [o] (every? #(contains? des (:db/id %)) (:form/defines (d/entity db o)))) olds)
        order (or (when fe (:form/order (d/entity db fe)))
                  order
                  (when (seq superseded) (apply min (map #(:form/order (d/entity db %)) superseded)))
                  next-order)
        lead (or (:lead acct) (some #(:form/lead (d/entity db %)) superseded))]
    (vec (concat
           (for [n (into #{ns} (map #(symbol (namespace (:var %)))) defs)] {:db/id (ns-tid n) :ns/name n})
           [(form-tx id (assoc acct :order order :lead lead :defines dkeys) eids)]
           (map #(def-ref [:var %] (eids [:var %])) declares)
           (mapcat (fn [{v :var :keys [kind contract doc]}] (def-tx db [:var v] (eids [:var v]) {:form id :kind kind :contract contract :doc doc})) defs)
           (mapcat #(def-tx db % (eids %) {:form id}) (filter (comp #{:method :impl} first) dkeys))
           (when ns-form? [{:db/id (ns-tid ns) :ns/form (form-tid id)}])
           (for [o superseded] [:db/retractEntity o])))))
"}

{:printed "nil",
 :form "(clojure.repl/source seon.program/def-keys)",
 :out
   "(defn- def-keys
  \"The definition keys account acct makes: its vars, methods, extensions and, for an ns
  form, its namespace.\"
  {:malli/schema [:=> [:cat :map] [:vector :any]]}
  [{:keys [ns ns-form? defs methods impls]}]
  (vec (concat (for [{v :var} defs] [:var v])
               (for [{:keys [multi dispatch]} methods] [:method multi dispatch])
               (for [{:keys [protocol type]} impls] [:impl protocol type])
               (when ns-form? [[:ns ns]]))))
"}

{:printed "nil",
 :form "(clojure.repl/source seon.program/account)",
 :out
   "(defn account
  \"The program account of one top-level form, or nil when it is none of the program's.
  opts: :nodes (each analyzed unit's node; or :units, their unit-accounts), :src (its exact text), :form
  (src as the reader read it: macro-uses walks it, so the text is read once), :ns (the namespace
  it was evaluated in), :ns-after (where it left the REPL), :ns-form? (it is an `ns` form:
  its head resolves to clojure.core/ns), :before (readback: var -> root before; nil for an
  analysis without running: every top-level def counts), :ran? (the form returned; a form
  that threw records only the vars it set), :ns-meta (an ns form's name's metadata: Jolt's
  ns drops it, jolt/ns-meta), :lead, :order, :k (occurrence of its text).\"
  {:malli/schema [:=> [:cat [:map [:src :string] [:form :any]]] [:maybe :map]]}
  [{:keys [nodes units src form ns ns-after ns-form? ns-meta before ran? lead order k] :or {k 0}}]
  (let [units (or units (map unit-account nodes))
        nsym (if ns-form? ns-after ns)
        nsx (find-ns nsym)
        a (merge-accounts units)
        types? (boolean (some #(= 'clojure.core/make-deftype-ctor (:init %)) (:defs a)))
        set? (fn [{v :var :as d}] (or (nil? before) (not (identical? (get before v) (root-of v))) (:macro? d)))
        defs (vec (for [d (:defs a)
                        :let [v (find-var (:var d))
                              multi? (contains? (:multis a) (:var d))]
                        :when (and (not (and (:declare? d) (not multi?))) (set? d))]
                    (cond-> {:var (:var d) :kind (def-kind v d multi? types?)}
                      (contract-text v d) (assoc :contract (contract-text v d))
                      (string? (or (some-> v meta :doc) (get (:meta d) :doc))) (assoc :doc (or (some-> v meta :doc) (get (:meta d) :doc))))))
        declares (into #{} (comp (filter :declare?) (map :var) (remove (set (map :var defs)))
                                 (remove #(contains? (:multis a) %))) (:defs a))
        methods (when (or ran? (nil? before))
                  (vec (for [{:keys [multi dispatch]} (:methods a)
                             :let [mv (when (and nsx (symbol? multi)) (ns-resolve nsx multi))]
                             :when (var? mv)]
                         {:multi (symbol mv) :dispatch (sedn/encode dispatch)})))
        impls (when (or ran? (nil? before)) (vec (distinct (:impls a))))]
    (when (and nsx (not (scratch-ns? nsx)) (not (:scratch ns-meta))
               (or ns-form? (seq defs) (seq declares) (seq methods) (seq impls) (:env? a)))
      (cond-> {:id (form-id nsym src k) :src src :ns nsym :ns-form? (boolean ns-form?)
               :defs defs :declares declares :methods (or methods []) :impls (or impls [])
               :refs (into (:refs a) (macro-uses nsx form)) :requires (:requires a) :banned (:banned a) :inline-defs (:inline-defs a)
               :timeouts (:timeouts a) :catches (:catches a)}
        lead (assoc :lead lead)
        order (assoc :order order)))))
"}
